clue.text: The distortion surrounding article is dramatic

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for distortion is put around the article, so it encloses it

parts.note: spin is a distorted, slanted presentation of the facts
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a piece of distorted reporting is melodramatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespian as an adjective means relating to drama and the theatre, a synonym of dramatic.

clue.text: In short term, a head steps in for one of the staff

indicators.note: the word for a head steps inside the shortened term
the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a school term
each means per head, a head, as in ten pounds each

explanation.surface: Midway through a school term, a headteacher fills in for a member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' looks like a headteacher but means per head, EACH; 'short' trims TERM to TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher is a member of a school's staff, so one of the staff describes it.

clue.text: Farm animal's directions, going North or South

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read the same going up or going down the grid

parts.note: E, W and E are the compass points east, west and east

explanation.surface: A farmer gives directions to a sheep, which wanders north or south.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, a farm animal.

clue.text: Hardships resulting from pressure on four dividing supplies

indicators.note: the numeral splits the word for supplies by going into it

parts.note: rations are allotted food supplies
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Hardships come from pressure on a family of four sharing out supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Privations are hardships caused by a lack of the necessities of life.

clue.text: Room for improvement? Recognition of achievement

definitions.meaning: a hospital ward, a room where patients get better
a prize given for something achieved

explanation.surface: An appraisal says there is still room to improve and praises an achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward is a hospital room for recovery, and an award honours an achievement.

clue.text: Destructive type in London museum left

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

explanation.surface: A wrecker is let loose inside a famous London museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is a person who wantonly damages property, a destructive sort of person.

clue.text: A princess in operetta or opera

parts.note: Princess Ida is the title character of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta

explanation.surface: Asking whether a princess appears in a light operetta or in grand opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan were a Victorian partnership writing comic operettas; Princess Ida is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is the famous Verdi opera about an Ethiopian princess.

clue.text: Arrive at station with train, where visitors are welcomed

parts.note: a train draws in when it arrives at a station
to groom someone is to train or prepare them

explanation.surface: Arriving at a station on a train, met by a welcoming committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like the railway vehicle, but it is a verb meaning to prepare, GROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing room is a formal room in a house in which guests are received.

clue.text: React aggressively in US city and yell

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
to shout is to yell

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper in an American city and screams.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to attack suddenly, physically or verbally.

clue.text: Nobody besides Evelyn was in this group of writers

definitions.text: Nobody besides Evelyn was in this group of writers

parts.words: Nobody besides Evelyn was in this group of writers
parts.note: seems to say no one but Evelyn belonged, but Evelyn is John Evelyn the seventeenth-century journal keeper, and Nobody is Pooter of the comic novel The Diary of a Nobody

explanation.surface: Apparently a claim that only one man, Evelyn, belonged to a literary circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobody' reads as no person, but it is the fictional Charles Pooter, whose daily journal was published as The Diary of a Nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn and the fictional Nobody both kept daily journals, so both belong among keepers of daily records.

clue.text: People inappropriately named, having Asian race in mind mistakenly

indicators.note: done mistakenly, the fodder words are put in a wrong, jumbled order

explanation.surface: A remark about a people misnamed because someone thought they were an Asian race.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is apt: Columbus believed he had reached the Indies, so the native peoples of America were wrongly called Indians, exactly the Asian mix-up the surface describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous peoples of the Americas were named Indians in error, after explorers thought they had reached India.

clue.text: Helpless under influence of drugs but not alcohol

parts.note: someone high is under the influence of drugs
but in the sense of and also, adding one thing to another
dry means free of alcohol, as in a dry town

explanation.surface: Someone is incapacitated by drugs although they have drunk nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Left high and dry is an idiom for stranded and helpless, like a ship beached by the tide.

clue.text: Jack, say, taking ill, getting worse

indicators.note: taking ill, badly, means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: iller is a jocular comparative of ill, meaning worse in health

explanation.surface: A man falls sick and his condition deteriorates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' reads as sick but works as badly, the anagram signal, turning TAKING into GIANTK; 'getting' links to ILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack of the beanstalk tale slew a giant, so he is an example of one who kills giants.

clue.text: Group of spies associated with ring for so long

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: Spies tied up with a ring have been operating for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is an Italian farewell, and so long is an informal way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Popular comrade reformed movement out of control

indicators.note: the letters of comrade are formed again in a new order

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitching movement

explanation.surface: A fellow socialist changes, and a political movement runs riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Democratic means of or for the ordinary people, as popular does.

clue.text: Again order kind of ale and S sort of gin

parts.note: real ale is a kind of traditionally brewed beer

indicators.note: a sort of gin suggests the letters of gin rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A barman orders another round of a certain ale and a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a stray S between 'and' and 'sort' which plays no part; REAL plus IGN, the anagram of GIN, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to put into order or alignment again, so again order describes it.

clue.text: Gewgaw odd kings removed for short spell

definitions.text: Gewgaw odd kings removed for short spell

indicators.note: those letters are taken away from the usual spelling

parts.note: a gewgaw is a trinket or bauble
K is the chess abbreviation for king; the odd ones are the first and third of the four Ks

explanation.surface: A trinket's king figures are taken away for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for short spell' means as a shorter spelling, not a brief period: dropping the first and third Ks from KNICKKNACK gives this variant.
explanation.definitionFit: This shorter spelling of knick-knack names a small worthless ornament, a gewgaw.

clue.text: Hunt the writer, in way that's cunning

indicators.note: the writer's name goes inside the abbreviation for way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Leigh Hunt was a nineteenth-century English essayist and poet

explanation.surface: An order to track down an author by some crafty method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunt' looks like a verb meaning to pursue, but it is the surname of the writer Leigh Hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is a noun meaning cunning or dexterity, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: 21, certainly not 11

parts.note: 21 is a vessel and 11 means stranded out of the water; this famous vessel ended up at the bottom of the sea, the opposite of being left stranded

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: one vessel that was definitely not left stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer 21 is SHIP and answer 11 is HIGH AND DRY; the liner that sank in 1912 was anything but beached.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean liner that famously sank on its maiden voyage was a ship that ended up deep underwater.

clue.text: One drunk upset another, see

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, turns the word upside down so it reads upwards

parts.note: another drunk, a sot
to spot is to see

explanation.surface: One drunkard upsets another, look.
explanation.definitionFit: A tosspot is an old word for a habitual drinker.

clue.text: In conceitedness, how offensive one is!

definitions.text: In conceitedness, how offensive one is!

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words conceitedness, how offensive

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how offensive a conceited person can be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a boastful person is exactly one who is offensive in conceitedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A boaster who flaunts himself is conceited and often offensive, which the exclamation describes.

clue.text: Finishing first, with low grade on a second exam

parts.note: F is a failing grade
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Someone completes a resit quickly after a poor mark on the first exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest finisher is the one who crosses the line first.

clue.text: In a word, final indication of rank or position in part of navy

definitions.text: In a word, final indication of rank or position
definitions.meaning: the suffix that ends words like lordship and professorship, signalling a rank or position
a vessel, one unit of a navy

explanation.surface: A naval officer explains how a word ending marks rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A navy is made up of ships, and the suffix -ship at the end of a word denotes a rank or office.

clue.text: Intermixes wildly as last resort

indicators.note: the letters of intermixes are shaken up wildly into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stirs ingredients together frantically as a final desperate measure.
explanation.definitionFit: In extremis is Latin for in extreme circumstances, when only a last resort remains.

clue.text: Element that makes one cross, turning up before noon

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned so it reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that irritates a person, appearing just before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry but it is the letter X; ONE reversed by 'turning up' gives ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a chemical element, a noble gas.

clue.text: Religious work I pore over

parts.note: to con is to study closely, pore over

explanation.surface: Someone studies a sacred painting closely.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a sacred painted image venerated in the Orthodox church.

clue.text: Officer in charge, captured by European artist

indicators.note: the abbreviation is caught inside the word for the European

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
John Constable was an English landscape painter

explanation.surface: An officer in command is taken prisoner by a European painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Officer' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition; 'artist' is the painter Constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A police constable is the lowest rank of police officer in Britain.

clue.text: Negative reaction that's repeated in error

definitions.meaning: a noise of disapproval from an audience
doubled, the word gives ...-..., a slang term for a blunder

explanation.surface: A jeer that someone mistakenly repeats.
explanation.definitionFit: A boo is a jeer of disapproval, and doubled it makes the slang word for a mistake.

clue.text: What's the welcoming king on?

indicators.note: the word the welcomes the following pieces into its middle

parts.note: R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what seat a king sits on while receiving guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well: a king sits on his seat of state while welcoming visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch sits on his ceremonial chair of state, so that is what the king is on.

clue.text: Quickly produce decisive result

definitions.meaning: to ... a piece of work is to produce it rapidly
in boxing, a blow that ends the fight outright

explanation.definitionFit: To knock out a draft is to dash it off; a knockout ends a contest conclusively.
